name: compactWheel
note: CompactForklift tyre. CylinderGeometry(0.32,0.32,0.24,20) - a plain drum, drawn through a 4-instance InstancedMesh and the ONLY round silhouette on an otherwise all-box model. Redesign as a cushion tyre on a recessed steel rim: near-full-width flat tread, tight shoulder round-over in the outer 55 mm, a flat bead sidewall, a rim flange at the widest axial face, and a dished hub pan with a centre boss. Envelope pinned: max radius 0.320 (the spin integrator's divisor AND the ground-contact radius), y half-extent 0.120.

name: compactWheelTreadStudy
note: A/B on tread width only, both with the same hub pan and rim flange. BEFORE holds full radius over just +/-20 mm (a balloon/motorcycle section); AFTER holds it over +/-64 mm (a cushion-tyre section). Same envelope, same vertex count - this decides which one a forklift actually has.

name: compactWheelAt8m
note: Same swap, framed at 8 m - the distance a walking camera passes a forklift. The bar is that the shoulder round-over and hub pan still read here, not just in a close-up.

name: compactBeacon
note: CompactForklift rotating beacon. CylinderGeometry(0.08,0.08,0.13,10) - a flat-topped drum at y=2.19, the highest point on the vehicle and the one part read against open sky. The cab roof top is at y=2.13, i.e. local y=-0.06, so everything below that is buried and any detail spent there is invisible; and at in-scene distance the whole lamp is under ten pixels tall, so fresnel rings would be a mathematical no-op. The budget is the SILHOUETTE above the roof line: a narrow mounting collar, a lens skirt flaring to full radius, a straight barrel, and a dome. Envelope pinned: max radius 0.080, y half-extent 0.065.

name: compactSteeringWheelREJECTED
note: DESIGNED, RENDERED, REJECTED - the TypeScript is deliberately left as TorusGeometry(0.13,0.018,6,14). BEFORE here is the exact lathe equivalent of that torus (tube section sampled at the same six angles), so both variants are measured in one axis frame. AFTER is the second of two dished-wheel designs: v1 put a conical spoke web level with the rim, v2 (this one) drops the web to a flat plate 28 mm behind the rim front with a proud hub cap. BOTH render as a solid lid, not a wheel - a steering wheel's defining features are its spokes, its hub and the OPEN sectors between them, and none of those is a surface of revolution. The envelope makes it worse: 0.148 radius against 0.0156 half-thickness is 1:19, so no lathe dish is deep enough to separate rim from web, and LatheGeometry's normals are averaged along the whole profile, which blurs the one step that might have read. The hoop at least keeps the hole, which is the wheel's entire silhouette. Anything better needs a hand-built spoked BufferGeometry, which is out of proportion for a 0.3 m part seen through 0.5-opacity glass on the low-quality LOD only.

name: operatorHatCrown
note: SeatedVehicleOperator hard-hat crown, shared by both forklift operators (scale 0.68) and the truck-bay drivers (scale 1.28). CylinderGeometry(0.13,0.145,0.1,18) - a flat-topped truncated cone, i.e. a bucket. The hat is the single most identifiable thing about a figure in a cab. Redesign: a steep skirt that seats into the brim, a shoulder, and a dome. Envelope pinned: max radius 0.145, y half-extent 0.050.

name: operatorHatCrownAt8m
note: Same swap at the forklift's 0.68 operator scale, framed at 8 m. A 0.197 m hat at 8 m is the honest test of whether the dome carries.

name: operatorHatBrim
note: SeatedVehicleOperator hard-hat brim. CylinderGeometry(0.18,0.18,0.025,18) - a flat disc, a frisbee. Redesign: a flat crown seat, a brim that falls away outward, a duck-bill turn-up at the edge and a rolled rim underside. Profile is wound underside-centre -> rim -> top-centre (increasing y) so LatheGeometry's analytic normals face OUT; the reverse winding previews identically in Workbench, which draws backfaces, and then renders inside-out on a FrontSide material. Envelope pinned: max radius 0.180, y half-extent 0.0125.

name: operatorHead
note: SeatedVehicleOperator head. SphereGeometry(0.12,16,12) - a ball sitting straight on the torso box with no neck at all. The hard-hat brim sits 0.06 above the head centre and its underside occludes everything above local y ~= +0.053, so the entire design budget belongs to the band below that: neck, jaw, cheek, temple. Redesign: neck column rising off the shoulders, jaw underside, jaw angle, cheek, and the widest ring moved down to +0.020 so the temple is the widest VISIBLE point. The bottom still converges on the axis, so the head meets the torso top at a point rather than on a coplanar disc that would z-fight. Envelope pinned: max radius 0.120, y half-extent 0.120.
